=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur
Background: The Brihadeeswarar Temple, built by Raja Raja Chola I in 1010 CE, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site dedicated to Shiva. Its walls display exceptional Chola-era sculptures including 81 classical Nataraja karanas.

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Figure with four arms performing the Ananda Tandava. Upper right holds a damaru drum, upper left holds a flame. Lower right shows Abhaya mudra, lower left points to raised left foot. Standing on Apasmara Purusha dwarf. Ring of flames encircles the figure. Crescent moon in spread hair.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Nataraja — Shiva as the Lord of Cosmic Dance

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nataraja: Nataraja is a depiction of Shiva as the divine cosmic dancer, with four arms, drum, fire, abhaya mudra, raised foot, and Apasmara.
https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/39328: Chola-period Nataraja bronzes exemplify the mature iconographic tradition with drum, fire, abhaya mudra, raised foot, and Apasmara all present.
https://www.ciis.edu/nataraja: The dance represents the five cosmic acts: creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and grace.

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
Who is this dancing figure and what does the dance mean?

=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai
Background: The Meenakshi Amman Temple is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (a form of Parvati) and her consort Sundareswarar (Shiva). It features 14 gopurams covered in thousands of stucco sculptures.

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Seated figure with elephant head and single tusk (left tusk broken). Four arms: upper right holds noose (pasha), upper left holds goad (ankusha), lower right holds broken tusk, lower left holds bowl of modaka sweets. Large round belly. Small mouse (mushika) visible near feet. Seated in lalitasana on lotus pedestal. Cobra wrapped around waist.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Ganesha — the elephant-headed son of Shiva and Parvati

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganesha: Ganesha is widely revered as the remover of obstacles, patron of arts and sciences, son of Shiva and Parvati.
https://www.himalayanacademy.com/view/what-ganesha-holds: The four arms typically hold the pasha, ankusha, broken tusk, and modaka. Each attribute carries symbolic meaning.
https://www.exoticindiaart.com/article/ganesha/: The mouse as vehicle represents the mind that gnaws at obstacles. The broken tusk was used to write the Mahabharata.

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
Who is this elephant-headed figure?

=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai
Background: The Meenakshi Amman Temple is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi and Sundareswarar (Shiva).

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Youthful figure with six arms. Holds a long vel (spear) in right hand. Peacock feather crown. A peacock (mayura) stands at the base. Two female figures (consorts) on either side.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Murugan (Kartikeya) — Tamil god of war and divine knowledge

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kartikeya: Kartikeya is identified by his vel (spear) and his vahana the peacock.
https://www.tamilnadu.gov.in/murugan: The vel symbolises divine knowledge piercing through ignorance.
https://www.templesofindia.co.in/murugan-iconography: Murugan's peacock vahana symbolises beauty and the destruction of ego.

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
Who is this youthful figure with a spear and peacock?

=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur
Background: The south face of Chola vimanas traditionally shows Dakshinamurthy, Shiva as the silent teacher.

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Seated figure facing south under a carved banyan tree. Four arms: right hands form Chin mudra (forefinger touching thumb) and hold a book. Left hands hold a flame and a serpent. Four small sages (rishis) sit at the feet. Expression is serene and inward-looking. One leg pendant, one folded.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Dakshinamurthy — Shiva as the silent teacher

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakshinamurthy: Dakshinamurthy is an aspect of Shiva as guru, representing supreme awareness and knowledge.
https://www.adishankara.org/dakshinamurthy-stotram: The Chin mudra communicates the highest Vedantic teaching without words.
https://www.ciis.edu/dakshinamurthy: Carved on the south face of Shiva temple vimanas, holding book, flame, and forming Cin mudra indicating oneness of self and Brahman.

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
Who is the seated teacher figure on the south wall?

=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram
Background: The Shore Temple contains three shrines with Pallava-era sculptures. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Figure with four arms. Elaborate crown. Upper arms raised but attributes are worn. Lower right may hold a discus or a spear — unclear. Lower left appears to hold a conch or a flower. No vahana visible at base. Samabhanga posture.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Unknown — possibly Vishnu or Murugan (attribute unclear)

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu: Vishnu is identified by the Sudarshana Chakra disc and Panchajanya conch. The chakra is the most reliable identifier.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kartikeya: Murugan's primary attribute is the vel (spear), not the chakra. The peacock vahana is definitive when present.

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
Is this Vishnu or Murugan? The upper hands are hard to see in my photo.

=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Brihadeeswara Temple, Gangaikonda Cholapuram
Background: Built by Rajendra Chola I in 1035 CE, similar in style to Thanjavur.

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Four-armed figure in dancing pose. Two references describe different identities. One mentions this could be a local form of Bhairava (fierce aspect of Shiva), another says it is Nataraja.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Nataraja or Bhairava — conflicting observations

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhairava: Bhairava is a fierce manifestation of Shiva, often depicted with weapons, dogs, and skulls. He does not typically carry a damaru in dance form.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nataraja: Nataraja is the benign cosmic dancer with damaru and flame.

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
Is this Nataraja or Bhairava? I am confused by the conflicting descriptions.

=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Nataraja Temple, Chidambaram
Background: The Chidambaram Nataraja Temple is the most important Nataraja shrine in India, the canonical home of Shiva's cosmic dance.

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Four-armed figure in Ananda Tandava. Damaru upper right. Flame upper left. Raised left foot. Apasmara at base. Prabhavali (ring of flames). Crescent moon in spread hair. Five-headed cobra visible in hair.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Nataraja — Shiva as Lord of Cosmic Dance (Chidambaram tradition)

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nataraja: First canonised in bronze at Chidambaram. All five canonical attributes are present.
https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/39328: The Chola-period Nataraja bronzes are the definitive iconographic form.
https://www.ciis.edu/nataraja: The Chidambaram temple houses the original Nataraja tradition.

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
This is from the Nataraja temple itself — can you confirm who this is?

=== TEMPLE CONTEXT ===
Temple: Ekambareswarar Temple, Kanchipuram
Background: One of the five Shiva temples representing the five elements. Represents earth (prithvi).

=== SCULPTURE OBSERVATIONS ===
Figure seated beneath a mango tree. Two smaller figures at the feet. Right hand in a gesture pointing upward. Expression serene. Cannot clearly see left hand attributes.

=== CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION ===
Possibly Shiva in teaching aspect — possibly Dakshinamurthy variant or local form

=== RETRIEVED HERITAGE REFERENCES ===
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakshinamurthy: Dakshinamurthy sits under a banyan tree (not mango), with rishis at feet, forming Chin mudra.
(The mango tree and Ekambareswarar temple are associated with Shiva-Parvati legend, but no specific sculpture documentation found)

=== INVESTIGATION QUESTION ===
Who is this seated teacher figure under the mango tree?
